messages.text:
ECAL-TESTS-CALOTECH assessed at `3af5538faf884d0abce98b0956c0e6d4f45d4527`, read-only. Recommendations sent directly to SoftEng.

The proposed narrow-edge family is a consistent **prototype**:

- `(N−1)` full 94 mm PCBs plus two 46 mm PCBs and 2 mm gaps preserve the original total row span exactly.
- With original span half-width `H=48N−1`, edge-board centres are `±(H−23)`; interior full-board centres are the original centres shifted 48 mm, omitting the final column.
- The 42 mm silicon and 40 mm active width preserve 2 mm PCB margins and 1 mm guards. Two ASIC packages at local `(u,v)=(0,±22)` fit comfortably; retain their complete thermal/material stacks.

I ran the pinned pad-mask implementation: **128 electrodes**, total active area **3520 mm²**, minimum electrode area **19.25 mm²**, keys `x=−4..3`, `y=−8..7`. Two 64-channel ASICs suffice. Emit partial-pad geometry/reference positions through the EdgeGrid cell table.

Material changes per board row are predictable:

| Quantity | Candidate minus baseline |
|---|---:|
| PCB area | −188 mm² |
| Total wafer area | −540 mm² |
| Sensitive area | −704 mm² |
| Passive guard area | +164 mm² |
| ASIC/package count | unchanged |

Important implementation constraints:

1. Nine physical boards on formerly eight-column layers exceed the original row stride of eight. Renumber within the existing 10-bit module field.
2. EdgeGrid mask keys omit layer. Assign separate module-ID ranges to different mask families; endcap phase families also need distinct IDs.
3. A direct 48 mm axial shift loses one row in each 276/468 mm short slab. Retaining their original 2/4 rows requires a smaller repacking shift, at most 33 mm here; record the actual phase.
4. Normalize endcap tangential phases modulo 96 mm to avoid missing edge boards from finite grid limits. Radial half-phasing requires the new inner partial row and all existing minimum-area, width, guard, ASIC-fit and aperture checks.
5. Preserve existing cooling runs where feasible and regroup interfaces using actual channel counts.

Before transport, screen dense impact maps for active-layer count, longest missing-layer streak, area/material changes, service bays, sector seams and transitions. Verify native overlaps, IDs and material totals. Geometric coverage remains a screening observable; improvement in response width requires the matched electron transport test.

No edits, native runs, performance claims or engineering acceptance.
